item.title: Dancing With the Stars Season 35 Features Super Bowl-Themed Performances and Elimination
item.description: Dancing With the Stars Season 35 aired its Super Bowl Night episode, marking the show's first-ever celebration of the Super Bowl. Contestants performed dances inspired by past Super Bowl halftime shows, paying homage to artists such as J Balvin, Shakira, Nelly, Bad Bunny, Usher, Bruno Mars, Lady Gaga, Jennifer Lopez, Rihanna, and the Black Eyed Peas. item.title: Florence Thompson, Subject of 'Migrant Mother' Photograph, Reflects on Legacy in 1978 Interview
item.description: Florence Owens Thompson, known as the 'Migrant Mother' in Dorothea Lange's 1936 photograph, held a framed copy of the iconic image during a 1978 interview after her identity was revealed. The photograph, taken in March 1936 while Thompson was a 32-year-old Cherokee mother of seven stranded at a migrant pea-pickers' camp in Nipomo, California, became one of the most recognized images of the Great Depression. Lange, working for the U.S. government's Resettlement Administration, captured Thompson's worried expression as her children shielded their faces. The photo prompted immediate federal aid, including 20,000 pounds of food for the camp, but Thompson never received compensation despite the image's global recognition. For over 40 years, Thompson remained anonymous, working multiple jobs to support her family. In 1978, a reporter from The Modesto Bee located her, leading to the 1978 photograph. item.title: Brazilian Singer Luiza Girardello Unveils Debut Album 'World Ablaze' at NYC Show
item.description: Brazilian singer-songwriter Luiza Girardello, a Berklee graduate, recently performed an intimate pocket show at Bibliotheque NYC to promote her debut album 'World Ablaze,' released on August 14, 2026. The album's title is derived from a line in her song 'Drunk on You,' which explores a destructive romantic relationship using alcohol as a metaphor. Girardello's performance blended original songs with vibrant covers of American rock and Brazilian pop classics, including a haunting rendition of Nirvana's 'Heart-Shaped Box' and fresh takes on Brazilian hits 'Dê um Rolê' and 'Samba e Amor.' She was joined by guitarist Niko Malinowski and saxophonist Yuval Agam, collaborators from her Berklee days. The show also featured Brazilian pop musician Zabelê Gomes, Girardello's manager and mentor, who is the daughter of Brazilian rock group Novos Baianos members. item.title: Cait Conley shuts down Rep. Mike Lawler's attempt to deflect on domestic abuse during NY-17 debate
item.description: During a heated debate for New York's 17th congressional district, Republican Representative Mike Lawler (R-NY) faced a sharp rebuke from Democratic challenger Cait Conley when he attempted to deflect from questions about domestic abuse by attacking her financial ties to former New York Governor Eliot Spitzer. The exchange began when Conley criticized Lawler for defending Rep. Max Miller (R-OH), whose ex-wife has accused him of physical abuse. Lawler responded by accusing Conley of taking money from Spitzer, who resigned in 2008 after being found to have used a prostitution ring. Conley immediately cut him off, stating, 'I do not need you to mansplain to me what domestic abuse and sexual assault against women are, and the appropriate response,' and told him to 'sit over there.' item.title: Trump Administration Sees Pattern of Female Officials Leaving Amid Leadership Shakeup
item.description: President Donald Trump's second-term administration has experienced a significant pattern of female officials departing, either through resignation or dismissal, according to The New York Times. The latest departure is Kimberly Guilfoyle, who was removed as U.S. ambassador to Greece after reports she requested a donor cover a $100,000 American Express bill ahead of her confirmation vote. Trump stated he 'didn't like what I read' about her, though he acknowledged she 'was doing a good job.' Her exit follows a spring reshuffle where four of Trump's eight female cabinet-level officials resigned or were fired within three months. These included Attorney General Pam Bondi, Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer, Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, and Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard, all replaced by men. item.title: Karl Rove Critiques Trump's Campaign Strategy Amid GOP Midterm Challenges
item.description: Karl Rove, a veteran Republican strategist who served as a senior adviser to President George W. Bush, has criticized President Donald Trump's recent campaign activities in a Wall Street Journal op-ed. Rove argues that Trump's messaging over the past week failed to resonate with undecided voters, marking a significant setback for the Republican Party as they approach the 2026 midterm elections. The strategist highlighted several concerning developments that occurred during what he described as a 'troubling' week for the GOP. These included Trump's October 5 executive order allowing long-haul truckers to use dyed diesel, a fuel exempt from federal highway taxes, which Rove noted would likely be absorbed by existing farm and ranch customers rather than benefiting new voters. item.title: Study Links Declining Cognitive Skills to Digital Overuse and Educational Shifts
item.description: A recent analysis compiled by The Financial Times, drawing from multiple studies across various institutions, indicates a consistent decline in human intelligence metrics including attention spans, reasoning abilities, and problem-solving skills. The data spans from the University of Michigan's Monitoring the Future Study to OECD assessments, showing worldwide trends with the United States experiencing a more pronounced decline. For instance, the OECD's Program for International Student Assessment reveals that the proportion of individuals unable to apply mathematical reasoning has risen by 35% in the U.S. compared to a 25% global increase. These declines began around 2012, predating the pandemic, and correlate with the rise of smartphones, social media, and passive content consumption patterns. item.title: Justice Department insiders question legal basis of White House-driven antitrust probe into media networks
item.description: The White House played a significant role in initiating a Justice Department (DOJ) antitrust investigation into major television networks, according to sources familiar with the matter. The probe, which targets the networks' brief suspension of pooled presidential coverage following the exclusion of three news outlets from the White House, has raised concerns among DOJ insiders about its legal merits. Two former DOJ officials stated that the networks' actions are likely protected under the First Amendment, referencing a 1982 Supreme Court decision that extended constitutional safeguards to group boycotts conducted for political purposes. The White House reportedly pushed the DOJ to pursue the investigation after CNN, Politico, and MS NOW were barred from the White House by President Donald Trump. item.title: Federal Judge Finds Trump Officials Spread False Claims to Justify Firing FEMA CFO
item.description: A federal judge has ruled that top officials from the Trump administration, including Elon Musk and former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem, knowingly spread false information to justify the termination of Mary Comans, the former chief financial officer at the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). Judge William Fitzpatrick, in a ruling dated October 13, determined that Comans was fired on February 11, 2025, for allegedly approving millions in hotel room expenses for undocumented immigrants, but the spending was actually approved by others. The judge found that Comans had neither the authority nor the ability to halt grants sent to state and local governments. The firing was part of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) cuts overseen by Musk during the early days of President Donald Trump's second term, under an executive order that led to the dismantling of entire agencies and the termination of thousands of workers. item.title: White House Press Secretary's Bar Exam History Under Scrutiny After WSJ Report
item.description: Katie Zacharia, President Donald Trump's newly appointed White House Press Secretary, has faced scrutiny over her claims of being a licensed attorney after The Wall Street Journal reported she failed the California bar exam in 2011. According to the Journal, Zacharia took the bar exam after graduating from Pepperdine University School of Law but did not pass it. Her failure to pass the bar exam became apparent when searches for her name as a licensed attorney in California, Texas, and Washington, D.C. yielded no results under either her married or maiden name. Journalist Judd Legum had previously raised questions about her credentials in his Popular Information newsletter. When questioned about her bar exam status, Zacharia responded vaguely, stating, 'When I moved to China,' without providing further clarification. item.title: Real-time Economic Distribution Statistics Provide Timely Insights
item.description: The Realtime Inequality project offers the first timely statistics on how economic growth is distributed across different demographic groups. Developed by researchers Thomas Blanchet, Léonard Mouillet, Emmanuel Saez, and Gabriel Zucman, the platform aims to provide accessible and up-to-date data on income and wealth distribution. The website, built by Akcan Balkir and James Feng, serves as a resource for understanding economic inequality in real time. The project's methodology focuses on creating a transparent and easily understandable system for tracking economic disparities. By providing data on how economic growth is distributed, the initiative helps policymakers, researchers, and the public gain a clearer picture of economic trends. The platform is designed to be user-friendly, with a clean interface that allows for easy navigation and data exploration. item.title: Trump Voters Express Frustration Over Rising Costs Ahead of Midterms
item.description: Some Trump voters who supported him in the 2024 election are expressing frustration with the current economic situation, particularly regarding rising prices and stagnant wages. According to a New York Times report, voters in Iowa, Ohio, Maine, and Michigan—states with competitive Senate races—shared their concerns about the cost of living. A retired nurse in Maine told the president, 'you should be taking care of the people in your country,' reflecting widespread dissatisfaction. Rebecca Guerrette, an independent voter, criticized the economy and called the Iran war a 'waste of money,' noting that living costs have risen while paychecks have not kept pace. She indicated she might not vote in the upcoming Senate race between Susan Collins and Troy Jackson. item.description: The political landscape is shifting as Democrats increasingly target Republican seats that were previously considered safe, according to recent reports. Analysts note that several MAGA-aligned Republican incumbents, once seen as secure, are now facing significant challenges in their districts. These include Reps. John McGuire (R-VA) and Lauren Boebert (R-CO), who were not initially viewed as at risk during President Donald Trump's second term. item.title: William Stanford Davis, 'Abbott Elementary' Actor, Announces Memoir 'Don't Mess With the Fat Kid'
item.description: William Stanford Davis, known for his role as Mr. Johnson in the hit TV show 'Abbott Elementary,' has announced the publication of his memoir titled 'Don't Mess With the Fat Kid' through BenBella Books. The memoir, which will be released in hardcover, e-book, and audiobook formats, chronicles Davis' life and career, including his struggles with addiction and rejection, as well as his journey to securing his breakout role at the age of 70. The book is structured in three parts: the first details his childhood in the 1960s in St. Louis' Ville neighborhood, a predominantly Black community; the second follows his early adulthood as he moves to Jefferson City in the early 1970s; and the third covers his transition from addiction to a working actor, highlighting years of perseverance and rejection before landing his most prominent role. item.title: Democratic Pastors and Faith-Based Politics Challenge MAGA's Religious Dominance
item.description: The article discusses a growing shift in American politics where Democratic candidates, particularly those with strong Christian backgrounds, are increasingly openly discussing their faith, challenging the Republican Party's historical claim to represent Christian values. Pastor Paul Brandeis Raushenbush, speaking on the 'Coffee with Contrarians' podcast, explained that this trend is unsettling to the right wing, which had long assumed a monopoly on religious discourse in politics. He noted that Democratic candidates like James Talarico and Adam Hamilton, both seminary-trained, are 'driving people nuts' on the right by openly discussing their Christian faith, a practice that was less common since the days of Jimmy Carter. item.title: Comedian Kathy Griffin Details Ongoing Harassment from MAGA Supporters Over 2017 Trump Mask Incident
item.description: Comedian Kathy Griffin, 65, has revealed that her life has been significantly impacted by the ongoing obsession of MAGA supporters with a controversial photo she posted in 2017. The image, which showed Griffin holding a ketchup-covered Trump mask resembling a severed head, sparked a severe backlash from Trump supporters. Griffin stated that the controversy led to numerous death threats, FBI visits, a spot on the no-fly list, and a Justice Department investigation. She also mentioned that her mother believed she had joined a terrorist group, and she was later diagnosed with complex PTSD and panic attacks. Griffin claims that Trump, Jared Kushner, Donald Trump Jr., and Dan Scavino held meetings to discuss how to ruin her career, leaving her unable to work for seven years. Despite these challenges, Griffin's comedy career began to recover in 2023 with a successful Las Vegas show, where ticket sales exceeded her expectations. item.title: Union Leader Challenges GOP Ad for Misrepresenting His Comments on Medicare for All
item.description: Gregory Floyd, president of Teamsters Local 237, has issued a legal threat against a Republican-aligned group for misrepresenting his comments in a Maine Senate campaign ad. The ad, produced by The Maine Standard—a group connected to the Senate Leadership Fund—attributes to Floyd a statement criticizing Democratic Senate candidate Troy Jackson's support for Medicare for All, calling it a 'disaster' that would 'wipe out union-negotiated health insurance.' Floyd's attorney, Eyad Asad, sent a letter dated October 13 to Senate Leadership Fund Executive Director Alex Latcham, demanding the ad be removed immediately. The letter argues that Floyd never made the quoted statement and that the ad falsely suggests he condemned Jackson's policy by placing Jackson's name before the quote. Floyd told NBC News he was 'shocked' upon seeing the ad, having first encountered it through a local union leader. He clarified that his previous comments about Medicare for All, made in a 2019 CBS News interview,

item.title: Nostalgic Glimpse of 1980s Halloween Celebrations Through Vintage Photos
item.description: The article features a collection of vintage photographs capturing the essence of a Halloween party held in the early 1980s. These images showcase friends dressed in homemade costumes, featuring creative designs ranging from witches and monsters to popular pop-culture characters of the era. The photos highlight the vibrant decorations, big hair, bold makeup, and lively atmosphere that defined Halloween celebrations during that decade. The collection offers a nostalgic look at how Halloween parties were celebrated more than forty years ago, emphasizing the community-oriented and uncommercialized nature of the holiday during that time. The article is part of a series on vintage Halloween celebrations, with previous posts focusing on similar events from the 1960s and 1970s. The photographs provide a visual history of Halloween traditions, showing how costumes and decorations reflected the cultural trends of the 1980s. item.title: Trump Claims Canada Will Become 51st State at Arizona Rally, Sparks Outrage
item.description: President Donald Trump made a controversial statement at a campaign rally in Bullhead City, Arizona, on October 14, 2026, declaring that Canada would become the 51st state of the United States, similar to his previous remarks about Greenland. The statement, which was met with immediate backlash from social media users and political commentators, has raised concerns about Trump's mental state and the potential implications of his rhetoric. Trump's comment, 'Canada will become the 51st state,' was followed by a reference to Greenland, a territory he has also expressed interest in annexing. The rally, held at Laughlin/Bullhead International Airport, drew a crowd of supporters, but the president's remarks quickly became the focus of criticism. Social media users reacted with disbelief and concern, with many labeling Trump's comments as 'complete insanity' and 'deeply unwell.' item.title: Stephen Miller Expresses Concern Over Legal Vulnerability Despite Trump Pardons
item.description: Stephen Miller, the White House deputy chief of staff, has privately expressed fears that he could face legal consequences including imprisonment, even with President Donald Trump's pardons. According to a Zeteo profile highlighted by Marcy Wheeler of emptywheel, Miller has told associates that he believes local and state prosecutors are targeting him for a 'prison cell.' The report clarifies that federal pardons do not prevent state or local prosecutions, which is a key distinction Miller appears to be aware of. Miller's concerns extend beyond criminal charges to include potential civil lawsuits and congressional investigations. He has also voiced worries that a future Democratic administration might find ways to circumvent Trump's clemency. Additionally, Miller has complained about the left using 'lawfare' to financially drain him and his wife, Katie Miller, a podcaster and former Trump official. item.title: Former Texas House Speaker: GOP Candidates in Texas Show Signs of Anxiety Over Senate Race
item.description: Dade Phelan, the former Texas House speaker who led a conservative legislative agenda, has expressed deep concerns about the current state of the Texas Republican Party. In an interview with Texas Monthly, Phelan described a palpable sense of anxiety among Republican candidates across the state, stating that 'people are freaking out' and that he has never seen such serious concern before. Phelan, who was labeled a RINO (Republican in Name Only) after supporting the 2023 impeachment of Attorney General Ken Paxton, discussed the party's struggles in the upcoming Senate race between Paxton and Democratic state Rep. James Talarico. Phelan criticized the party's continued focus on divisive issues like transgender policies in sports, noting that such messaging fails to resonate with swing voters. item.title: Daddy Issues Season 3 Begins Filming with New Cast Members and Returning Stars
item.description: The BBC comedy series 'Daddy Issues' has commenced filming for its third and final season in Stockport, with the return of main cast members Aimee Lou Wood and David Morrissey. The show, created by Danielle Ward, follows the comedic misadventures of Gemma (Wood) and her father Malcolm (Morrissey) as they navigate family life, relationships, and unexpected challenges. This season introduces several new guest stars including Sian Gibson as Rita's sister Juno, Neil Morrissey as Malcolm's new friend Ellis, Shobna Gulati as the mysterious neighbor Odette, and Anthony Welsh as Gemma's love interest Avery. Returning cast members include Sarah Hadland as Rita, David Fynn as Derek, Taj Atwal as Cherry, and Sharon Rooney as Catherine. The series has been praised for its authentic portrayal of family dynamics and relatable humor. item.title: Trump-Associated Oil Company Sees Stock Surge Following Social Media Post on Greenland Drilling
item.description: A Texas-based oil company with ties to former President Donald Trump experienced a significant stock surge following a social media post made by Trump on Truth Social. The company, Greenland Energy, saw its shares jump 88 percent after Trump announced on the platform that 'Massive' oil, gas, and mineral exploration was 'getting ready to begin in our new and beautiful Greenland.' The post was made around midnight following a campaign event in Wasilla, Alaska, but provided no specific details about the projects or timeline. According to reports, Trump was likely referring to Greenland Energy's efforts to drill in Jameson Land, an area in eastern Greenland where executives claim up to $1 trillion in crude oil reserves may be located. The company's connections to Trump's inner circle are notable, with a board member involved in a defense firm working on Trump's 'Golden Dome' missile shield project, and board chair Larry Swets reportedly close to Trump. item.title: Global Health Insurance Costs Vary Widely: U.S. Ranks Highest, Morocco Lowest
item.description: The SIP Health Cost Index, released by Switzerland-based SIP Medical Family Office, provides a comprehensive analysis of private health insurance costs across 60 countries popular with expats. The 2026 study reveals the United States as the most expensive country for private healthcare, with an average annual premium of $23,987, followed by Hong Kong, Singapore, China, and the United Kingdom. Notably, Morocco emerged as the least expensive country for private healthcare at $7,609 annually, while Malta ranked among the most affordable options for American expats. The report highlights that medical inflation has driven an 18% average increase in private healthcare costs globally, with the U.S. and Saudi Arabia experiencing the highest jumps at 33%. In contrast, Japan and Greece saw minimal increases of 3% and 6%, respectively. item.title: Philippine-Italian Sales Alliance Targets Indie Film Buyers in Asia, Europe, and North America
item.description: Fire & Ice Media from the Philippines and Coccinelle Film Sales from Italy have formed a strategic partnership to promote independent films to international buyers across Asia, Europe, and North America. The alliance was unveiled at Busan's Asian Contents & Film Market, where the companies presented a curated selection of Filipino films. Fire & Ice Media, led by Abell Diño-Cabrera, handles film and TV development, production, and sales, while Coccinelle, founded by Francesca Breccia, specializes in selling independent films internationally. The partnership combines their regional expertise and buyer networks to secure distribution deals beyond home markets. Diño-Cabrera emphasized that every film has unique market potential, and the collaboration allows them to better serve filmmakers by leveraging complementary strengths. item.title: Commerce Secretary Lutnick's Plan to Evict Residents from Manhattan Hotel Fails
item.description: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's effort to clear longtime residents from the Pierre, a renowned Manhattan hotel and co-op, has collapsed after the proposed $2 billion sale fell through. The deal, which would have required all residents to sell their units and relocate, was championed by Lutnick, who owned a penthouse in the building and stood to profit significantly from the transaction. The would-be buyer, Saudi investor Motasem Khashoggi, failed to meet a $100 million deposit deadline, causing the sale to collapse. Lutnick, who had helped shape Khashoggi's proposal, was reportedly set to earn $60 million from his penthouse sale, while his former company, Newmark Group, would have received a $30 million advisory fee. Internal communications revealed Lutnick had agreed to offer an internship to Khashoggi's son at a brokerage linked to Cantor Fitzgerald, the firm he led. item.title: Texas GOP abandons gerrymandered House seat after strategic misstep
item.description: The Texas Republican Party's gerrymandering strategy has unraveled as the GOP abandons efforts to unseat Democratic Representative Henry Cuellar in a district they specifically redrawn to favor Republican gains. According to Punchbowl News, the Congressional Leadership Fund, a key Republican super PAC, is withdrawing millions in advertising funds from the race against Cuellar, redirecting resources elsewhere. This marks a significant reversal for the GOP, which had redrawn the heavily-Latino South Texas district to make it more Republican-leaning, a move that was part of a controversial mid-decade gerrymander endorsed by Donald Trump. The district was one of five redrawn to shift political dynamics in favor of Republicans, but election analysts argue the strategy was flawed from the outset. item.title: Senate Republican Urges Stronger Vaccination Efforts Amid Measles Outbreak
item.description: Senator Bill Cassidy, the Republican chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, has criticized the Trump administration for not promoting vaccinations vigorously enough during a significant measles outbreak in 2026. Cassidy, who is also a physician, emphasized the importance of vaccination during a CNN interview with Jake Tapper, stating, 'My concern as a physician is that everyone should be vaccinated for measles. And you may think it only affects me. That's not true because you infect other people.' He further explained, 'If I'm not protected, but you are, then I'm not exposed. I'm all about asking people to be immunized for yourself and for others.' The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reported that U.S. measles cases have surpassed 4,000 this year, with approximately 96% linked to known outbreaks. item.title: GTA 6 Leak Reveals Story Footage and Unexpected NSFW Elements
item.description: A recent leak from the anonymous source known as Cyberleek has provided a detailed look at Grand Theft Auto VI, featuring story clips, gameplay footage, and an unexpected NSFW element. The nearly 25-minute video, posted on social media, includes scenes of the male protagonist, Jason, walking around completely nude with full detail modeling. The video also contains brief footage of Lucia, the game's other protagonist, seen mostly nude at the end. While the nudity is a notable aspect, the leak also showcases various gameplay elements such as vehicular races, vehicle customization options, and first-person gameplay mode. The leak comes just weeks before the game's November 19 release date, with the game already available for preorder on Xbox Series X/S and PlayStation 5. item.title: Starship S40 Completes Round Trip Journey Through Space, Air, and Ocean
item.description: SpaceX's Starship S40 has successfully completed a round trip journey through space, air, and ocean, marking a significant milestone in the development of reusable spacecraft. The vehicle, which is part of SpaceX's Starship program, launched from the company's Starbase facility in Texas, reached orbit, and then returned to Earth, landing in the ocean. This successful test flight demonstrates the vehicle's ability to perform complex maneuvers and re-enter the atmosphere safely. The S40 is the fourth flight test of the Starship system, following previous tests that included both successful and unsuccessful attempts. This particular flight focused on testing the vehicle's ability to navigate through different environments, including space, air, and ocean, which is crucial for future missions to the Moon and Mars. The successful landing in the ocean is a key step toward achieving full reusability of the Starship system, which is a major goal for SpaceX. The company has been working on deve

item.title: Elon Musk Blames Trump for Ukraine Satellite Internet Restrictions After Deadly Incident
item.description: Elon Musk has publicly accused former U.S. President Donald Trump of being ultimately responsible for restrictions on Ukrainian troops' satellite internet access following a sudden slowdown that reportedly led to casualties. The controversy stems from SpaceX's decision to limit the speed of Starshield, the government version of Starlink satellite internet service used by Ukrainian military forces. Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov had urged Musk to lift the speed cap, citing the critical need for uninterrupted connectivity during military operations. Musk responded on X, stating that Starshield systems are controlled by the U.S. government and that any usage restrictions are decided by the U.S. military, with ultimate authority resting with the President. He clarified that Starlink, as a commercial service, is limited to civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military actions. item.title: Economic Analysis Suggests Trump's Inflation Trends May Persist
item.description: A recent analysis published by Raw Story highlights concerning economic trends under President Donald Trump's administration. The report details that September's inflation data showed a 3.7% annual increase in prices, with a 0.6% monthly rise representing one of the highest recent monthly increases. Simultaneously, worker wages decreased by 0.5%, creating a situation where the cost of goods is rising while the purchasing power of workers is declining. Jack Crosbie of Rolling Stone, cited in the analysis, describes this economic pattern as Trump's 'final indignity,' suggesting it has become a permanent fixture rather than a temporary issue. The analysis points to rising gas prices as a key driver of this trend, which could have significant implications for the upcoming midterm elections. Crosbie notes that the Federal Reserve may consider raising interest rates again in late October, just before the midterms, to combat inflation. item.title: Ohio Congressman's Lawyer Sent Cease-and-Desist Over Dog Medication and Divorce Threats
item.description: The lawyer for U.S. Representative Max Miller, a Republican from Ohio, has been accused of attempting to extort the ex-husband of Miller's girlfriend through a cease-and-desist letter that included allegations of animal cruelty and narcotics crimes. The letter, sent by attorney Larry Zukerman on behalf of Jaclyn Alatrash, Miller's girlfriend, accused Matthew Kampert, Alatrash's ex-husband, of giving his arthritic dog a steroid shot that allegedly caused the dog's death. The letter also threatened to reopen their divorce to seek spousal support and property, and claimed Kampert was working with Miller's ex-wife to damage the couple's reputations. Kampert denied the allegations, stating he administered a single steroid shot for arthritis pain to his 10-year-old dog Roo in 2021, which helped the dog move around, and that Roo died two years later. item.title: Former Trump Aide Denies Allegations of Misdirected Kennedy Center Donation
item.description: Ric Grenell, a former aide to former President Donald Trump, has strongly denied allegations that he misdirected a $6 million donation intended for the Kennedy Center. The dispute, which has escalated to the White House, involves former Trump attorney Alina Habba, who reportedly brought the accusation to President Trump in the Oval Office. According to Axios, Habba alleged that Grenell persuaded her husband, Turkish investor Turhan Mildon, to include a Kennedy Center donation in a $17.6 million payment related to a private business deal. She initially claimed the donation was $17 million but later revised it to $5.6 million. Grenell responded to the allegations on social media, calling them 'absurd' and demanding that Axios reporter Marc Caputo provide evidence. 'I've never asked for one cent to be sent somewhere else pretending it was for the Kennedy Center and I've never received any payment from him at all,' Grenell stated. item.title: CBS Foreign Editor Accuses Staff of Insubordination During Editorial Dispute
item.description: CBS News foreign editor Shayndi Raice, handpicked by CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss, reportedly held a virtual meeting with the network's foreign bureau where she accused staff of insubordination and threatened firings. According to a secretly recorded meeting provided to media watchdog Status, Raice defended editorial decisions regarding a recent Israel report, particularly a 'CBS Evening News' segment marking the Oct. 7 anniversary. She insisted the report was not interference, but warned that refusing to follow the chain of command 'is called insubordination, and it's legal grounds for firing.' An attendee described the meeting as a '15-minute tirade' with 'jaws on the floor' as Raice spoke. Correspondent Holly Williams challenged Raice over directives regarding her report, specifically noting concerns about the removal of allegations related to Benjamin Netanyahu being warned before the Oct. 7 attack. item.title: Political Operative Expands Spoiler Campaigns to Target GOP Senate Races
item.description: Aaron Day, a political operative known for helping cost Republican Senator Kelly Ayotte her 2016 reelection bid through a third-party campaign, is now leading efforts to deploy similar strategies across multiple states ahead of the 2026 midterms. According to a Semafor report, Day is channeling up to $2.5 million through his Stark Freedom PAC into targeted digital advertising campaigns, many generated using AI, to build name recognition for third-party candidates in Texas, Iowa, New Hampshire, Minnesota, South Carolina, Michigan, Ohio, and Kansas. The goal, as Day states, is to 'cost Republicans the Senate' by siphoning off conservative voters, particularly those who might otherwise support GOP candidates. His website explicitly states the aim of undermining Republican Senate prospects. Day claims his strategy is about holding Republicans 'accountable' rather than simply acting as a spoiler. item.title: Lisandro Martinez Criticizes Manchester United's Transfer Strategy Following Champions League Defeat
item.description: Lisandro Martinez, Manchester United's Argentine defender, has publicly criticized the club's summer transfer strategy after a 2-0 Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid. Martinez directly addressed football director Jason Wilcox, expressing frustration over the lack of significant reinforcements despite the club's £192 million spending on new signings including Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, and Andrey Santos. The loss, marked by a quick first-half goal from Pablo Barrios and a second-half strike by Ademola Lookman, was compounded by Leny Yoro's red card, extending United's winless streak to five matches across all competitions. Martinez emphasized the need for stronger squad reinforcement to compete with top European clubs, stating, 'I expect more from our technical director. I would have to be honest, as the players, we have to do more, but it's just important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.' item.title: EA Sports College Football Faces Financial Challenges and Monetization Concerns
item.description: EA Sports College Football, which returned to the market in 2024 after an 11-year hiatus, has become a commercial success, selling over 2 million copies in its first year and becoming the second-best-selling game in the U.S. for 2024. However, recent reports indicate growing concerns about the franchise's future. The game's success was driven by strong sales, with College Football 25 becoming the best-selling sports video game in U.S. history by dollar sales. Despite this, sales have gradually declined since 2024, with College Football 27 lasting only one month as a standalone title before being bundled with Madden NFL 27. The primary concern stems from rising costs, particularly the significant increase in Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL) payments to players. For College Football 25, EA paid $600 per player, totaling approximately $7-7.5 million for over 11,000 players. By College Football 27, this cost had jumped to $1,500 per player, totaling nearly $20 million. These costs, combined

item.title: Ukraine's President Zelensky: Russian Missile Strike on Kyiv Power Plant Without Western Warning
item.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that a Russian ballistic missile struck a power plant in Kyiv without prior warning from Western allies, resulting in at least two fatalities and approximately 20 injuries. The attack occurred shortly after U.S. President Donald Trump's announcement of an 'energy ceasefire' between Russia and Ukraine, which raised questions about the effectiveness of efforts to protect critical infrastructure. Zelensky criticized the lack of early warning, stating that Ukraine's systems detected the missiles only as they approached the city. The strike targeted the CHP-4 power plant, a key energy infrastructure facility, and also damaged a residential building in the Desnianskyi district. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko confirmed the casualties, noting that the attack was part of a broader pattern of Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. item.title: Jared Kushner Faces Lawsuit Over Unconfirmed Diplomatic Role and Financial Disclosure Concerns
item.description: Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump's son-in-law, is facing a federal lawsuit alleging he has wielded significant government power without Senate confirmation or proper financial disclosures. The lawsuit, filed by Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW) in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, claims Kushner has functioned as a key diplomat during Trump's second term, negotiating directly with foreign leaders on critical global conflicts involving Israel, Hamas, Ukraine, Russia, and Iran. The complaint details Kushner's meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and Iranian officials, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio testifying that he communicates with Kushner and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff approximately ten times daily. item.title: Republican Senate Candidate's $10 Gas Card Giveaway Draws Criticism Amid Iran War Fuel Price Debate
item.description: Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers' campaign faced criticism after his wife, Kristi Rogers, distributed $10 gas cards at a Detroit gas station on Wednesday. The giveaway, intended to highlight her husband's proposal to suspend Michigan's state gas tax, drew immediate backlash from critics who linked soaring fuel prices to President Donald Trump's ongoing conflict with Iran. Reporter Sam Robinson documented the event at the Freedom Fuel station, noting that customers expressed mixed reactions. Some praised the gesture as 'courageous' for engaging with the community, while others questioned the timing and relevance of the giveaway amid rising gas prices. Democratic strategist Connor Farrell mocked the stunt with a reference to 'Arrested Development,' asking, 'It's a gallon of gas, Michael. What could it cost, ten dollars?' item.title: Former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene Critiques MAGA Movement as 'Grotesque Cult' After Rally Incident
item.description: Former Congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene, once a staunch supporter of former President Donald Trump, has delivered a scathing critique of the MAGA movement, declaring it has deteriorated into a 'grotesque cult' following a recent incident at a Trump rally in Youngstown, Ohio. During the rally on October 12, 2026, a woman wearing a 'Release The Epstein Files' shirt was physically assaulted by multiple attendees, with Trump himself making derogatory remarks about her appearance, referring to her as a 'fat guy' who needed to 'go on a diet.' Greene, who has attended more Trump rallies than she can count, stated that the current MAGA movement has become unrecognizable from its original principles. She criticized the movement for now being dominated by individuals who emulate Trump's behavior, attacking women, mocking their appearance, and turning against victims of 'elites.' item.title: Iran's Attacks Threaten Trump's Efforts to Lower Prices Before Midterms
item.description: According to a CNN analysis published on October 14, 2026, Iran's renewed military actions in the Middle East are undermining President Donald Trump's last-minute strategy to reduce consumer prices ahead of the midterm elections. The report highlights that Iran, along with its proxies like the Houthis, is deliberately targeting oil shipments to maintain high oil prices, which directly impacts inflation rates. This timing coincides with the political pressure Trump and the Republican Party are facing as the midterms approach. The analysis by CNN's David Goldman states that Trump's push to deliver positive economic news has 'run face-first into a brick wall' due to these attacks. The situation has worsened as at least 18 vessels in the Middle East have been attacked over the past two weeks, causing oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz to drop to 54% of prewar levels. item.title: The Hidden Cost of Digital Convenience: How Small Tech Changes Create Irreversible Work
item.description: The article explores the concept of the 'luxury trap' as described in Yuval Noah Harari's 'Sapiens,' drawing parallels between historical agricultural practices and modern technological conveniences. The author argues that small, incremental changes—whether in farming or software development—become normalized over time, making it difficult to revert even when the long-term costs become apparent. In the farming example, early humans gradually adopted agriculture, which initially seemed beneficial but eventually led to a more labor-intensive lifestyle that became the new normal. Similarly, in software engineering, adding a simple retry mechanism to handle timeouts may seem helpful at first, but it creates dependencies that make reverting the change complex and costly. The author illustrates this with a code example where a payment system initially charged customers twice due to a lack of idempotency, requiring additional infrastructure to manage transaction keys. item.title: Guns N' Roses and Arnold Schwarzenegger Collaborate on 'Terminator 2' Theme Song in 1991
item.description: The collaboration between Guns N' Roses and Arnold Schwarzenegger for the 1991 single 'You Could Be Mine' represents a significant pop-culture crossover of the 1990s. The song served as the theme for the blockbuster film Terminator 2: Judgment Day. Director James Cameron sought a hard-rock track to reflect the rebellious nature of young John Connor, portrayed by Edward Furlong. Schwarzenegger personally invited the band to dinner at his home to negotiate the song's placement in the film. The band members, who were fans of Terminator, expressed their admiration for the franchise, while Schwarzenegger was a fan of their music. The music video, directed by Jeffrey Abelson and Andy Morahan, combined live concert footage of Guns N' Roses performing at the Ritz in New York City with cinematic scenes. In the video, Schwarzenegger's T-800 character arrives at the venue to eliminate the band, but after scanning them, decides it would be 'a waste of ammo' and walks away. The song was released in

item.title: Arizona County Voters Question Trump's Promises Amid Cost of Living Crisis
item.description: Residents in an Arizona county that Donald Trump won overwhelmingly in the 2024 election are expressing disillusionment with his administration, particularly regarding economic policies. Kandy Soto, a 66-year-old retiree and former Trump supporter, now relies on food banks after her husband's injury and rising grocery prices made life unaffordable. She represents a growing number of Trump voters who feel worse off economically since the 2024 election. The Atlantic's Yvonne Wingett Sanchez reported that nearly all Trump supporters interviewed felt financially strained, with many losing food assistance due to changes in Trump's tax legislation that limits benefits and penalizes states for administrative errors. Victoria Dombrowski, a mother of two, lost $800 monthly in food aid after struggling with the new renewal process. item.title: U.S. Ambassador Kimberly Guilfoyle Sought to Remove Controversial Report on Unpaid Restaurant Bill Before Resignation
item.description: U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle reportedly attempted to have a damaging news story removed from the Daily Mail prior to her resignation, according to a Wall Street Journal report. The story detailed an unpaid $1,768 restaurant bill at Matsuhisa, a Four Seasons restaurant in Vouliagmeni, Greece, where Guilfoyle dined with her son and his father on May 31. An aide reportedly called the restaurant to claim the meal was supposed to be free, and the bill was later sent to the U.S. Embassy. State Department officials requested proof of payment, but Guilfoyle did not provide it. Her resignation, announced by White House press secretary Katie Zacharia, ended a contentious tenure marked by controversy. The resignation follows a State Department inspector general investigation into allegations including possible substance abuse, unauthorized travel, improper gift acceptance, and a close relationship with an energy and construction firm. item.title: Lillian Gish: Iconic Silent Film Star and Fashion Pioneer of the 1920s
item.description: Lillian Gish (October 14, 1893 – February 27, 1993), an American actress renowned for her contributions to silent cinema, reached the peak of her fame during the 1920s. Known as the 'First Lady of American Cinema,' Gish's career spanned 75 years, from 1912 to 1987. Her work in the 1920s included starring in masterpieces directed by D.W. Griffith, such as Way Down East (1920), where she performed a perilous scene lying on an ice floe drifting toward a waterfall, causing permanent nerve damage. She also co-starred with her sister Dorothy Gish in Orphans of the Storm (1921), set during the French Revolution. Gish's influence extended beyond acting; she directed her own film, Remodeling Her Husband (1920), and was a prominent advocate for silent film as a universal visual language. Her fashion sense bridged traditional and modern styles, with portraits from the early 1920s showcasing her in avant-garde designs like Mariano Fortuny gowns. item.title: FBI Veterans Accuse Director Kash Patel of Misrepresenting Crime Statistics to Mask Decline in Case Referrals
item.description: FBI Director Kash Patel faces criticism from former FBI officials who accuse him of inflating crime statistics to mask a significant decline in the bureau's case referrals. According to a review of Justice Department data obtained by the watchdog group Justice Connection, the FBI has referred 15 percent fewer criminal cases for federal prosecution during Donald Trump's second term compared to the same period under President Joe Biden. The data also shows the bureau has made fewer referrals than it did at the same point in Trump's first term. Despite Patel's claims of a 90 percent increase in violent crime arrests, the FBI's reported figure of 54,000 arrests includes cases where FBI employees were merely present during state and local police arrests, a practice the bureau admits is not reflective of their own cases. item.title: GOP Lawmaker Threatens to Call Officer Over Press Recording During Debate
item.description: Rep. Andy Harris (R-MD), chair of the House Freedom Caucus, erupted in frustration during a post-debate press conference in Cambridge, Maryland, after being questioned by reporters about his performance. The incident occurred following a debate with Democratic challenger Dan Schwartz, where Harris faced audience laughter when explaining rising fuel prices. Harris accused reporters of being rude and demanded they stop recording him, claiming they were violating Maryland's two-party consent law for audio and video recordings. 'You do not have my permission to record!' Harris warned a reporter. 'If you record, we will refer you to the prosecutor!' When pressed on the legality of his claims, Harris insisted that Maryland law requires two-party consent for recordings, though legal experts noted that Maryland's wiretap law does not apply to public recordings, as evidenced by a 2010 court case where a motorcyclist was not charged for recording a traffic stop in public view. item.title: New Ministry MCERT Proposes 400 Job Cuts Amid Public Service Concerns
item.description: The newly formed Ministry for Cities, Environment, Regions and Transport (MCERT) has proposed cutting 400 roles as part of a restructuring effort. MCERT, established in July by merging several ministries, announced the plan during a meeting with staff on Wednesday. The ministry stated that 365 of the positions to be eliminated are currently vacant, with a total staff count of approximately 1700. The proposed cuts aim to generate $50 million in annual savings by 2028-29. Chief executive Jeremy Lightfoot emphasized that no final decisions have been made, and staff will have the opportunity to provide input before decisions are finalized in December. The announcement comes amid broader government plans to reduce public service jobs by 14% over three years, which would result in approximately 8700 job losses by mid-2029, with 3500 of those potentially affecting Wellington. item.title: Women Seeking Safety from Domestic Violence Arrested and Detained by ICE
item.description: The article details the case of Pilar, a 48-year-old woman who sought to escape a violent relationship with her boyfriend, only to be arrested and detained by ICE after reporting domestic violence to police. Despite her claims of physical and psychological abuse, including bruises and scratches, police sided with her boyfriend, who had recently become a U.S. permanent resident. The police report noted that the boyfriend's shirt was torn while Pilar's was not, suggesting she was not physically assaulted as she claimed. Pilar was arrested and held without bail, despite having no criminal history and a pending asylum case. ICE placed a detainer on her, leading to her detention. The article also discusses Leya, another woman who faced similar circumstances, arrested after a domestic dispute and later released on bond. Both cases highlight the chilling effect on immigrant victims of domestic violence, who fear reporting abuse due to the risk of deportation. The piece criticizes the practice

item.title: Armed Vigilantes Interrupt Child's Pajama Party Amid Trump-Era Mail-In Voting Dispute
item.description: The article details an incident where armed vigilantes, allegedly part of a pro-Trump movement, invaded the pajama party of a young girl in Harris County, Texas. The event occurred amid a broader conflict over mail-in voting, which has been a focal point of political tension since the 2020 election. County Commissioner Rodney Ellis, the first Black commissioner elected to the Harris County Board, became a target of false accusations regarding the alleged forging of 750,000 absentee ballots. These claims, promoted by Trump supporters and funded by wealthy conservative figures like Steven Hotze, led to a series of aggressive actions against Ellis and his family. Hotze, a wealthy right-wing figure, hired detectives to search for non-existent forged ballots, resulting in an incident where a repairman was confronted and threatened with a gun. The charges against Hotze were later dropped, with connections to Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, who has been actively involved in restricting mai

item.title: Orionid Meteor Shower Peaks Overnight October 21-22: How to Watch
item.description: The annual Orionid meteor shower is expected to peak overnight on Wednesday, October 21, into Thursday, October 22, according to NASA. The Orionids are known for producing fast, bright meteors that can leave glowing trails and, occasionally, striking fireballs. Under dark skies, the shower typically produces about 10 to 20 visible meteors per hour, although this year’s waxing gibbous moon may wash out some of the fainter streaks. Viewing conditions should improve after the moon sets and before dawn, so observers should check local moonset times when planning their outing. NASA advises watching after midnight from a location far from city lights and streetlights. No telescope or binoculars are necessary; a blanket or reclining chair, warm clothing, and about 30 minutes for eyes to adapt to the dark are enough. Viewers should look across a wide area of sky rather than focusing on a single point. Although the meteors appear to originate near the constellation Orion, they can streak across

item.title: White House officials express anger over press secretary's poor vetting process
item.description: The White House is reportedly experiencing internal anger following the debut of new Press Secretary Katie Zacharia, who struggled during her first press briefing. According to MS NOW host Joe Scarborough, the vetting process for Zacharia was the worst in a decade, comparing it to the Bernie Kerik appointment. Scarborough stated that White House officials were 'blindsided' by her performance and that they are now 'angry' about the decision. Co-host Jonathan Lemire added that Chief of Staff Susie Wiles was not consulted about the appointment, which came directly from President Trump. The report indicates that Zacharia had been strategically timing her media appearances on Newsmax and Fox News to catch Trump's attention after Karoline Leavitt announced her departure. The incident has raised questions about the quality of vetting for high-level White House positions and the influence of media appearances in presidential appointments. item.title: Obama Urges Democrats to Focus on State Legislative Races as Key to Shaping American Lives
item.description: Former President Barack Obama has emphasized the critical importance of state legislative races in shaping the daily lives of Americans, urging Democrats to prioritize these contests over congressional politics. In a fundraising email sent to supporters of the Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee (DLCC), Obama argued that state lawmakers often have a more direct impact on citizens' lives than federal officials. He highlighted that issues such as civil rights, fair representation, and election integrity are deeply rooted in statehouse decisions, drawing from his experience as a state senator in Illinois. Obama noted that the current political climate, marked by weakened democratic norms, makes state legislatures more crucial than ever for safeguarding the future of democracy. The email warned that Democrats have only 21 days to capitalize on a 'generational opportunity' to gain control of state legislatures ahead of the November 3 midterms. item.title: Michigan GOP Senate Candidate's Wife Led Controversial Military Contractor During Husband's Intelligence Committee Leadership
item.description: The wife of Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers held top leadership positions at Aegis Defence Services, a controversial private military contractor, while her husband chaired the House Intelligence Committee. According to a report by Drop Site News, Kristi Rogers (formerly Kristi Clemens) became CEO of Aegis in 2009 and served as vice chair by 2011, the year after she married Mike Rogers. During Mike Rogers' tenure as chairman of the House Intelligence Committee starting in January 2011, Aegis secured significant U.S. government contracts, including a $1.017 billion contract to secure the U.S. Embassy in Kabul, Afghanistan. The report notes that the couple's wealth grew substantially during this period, with investment income rising as Mike Rogers chaired the committee. House rules do not require lawmakers to disclose their spouses' salaries, so the financial details of Kristi Rogers' role at Aegis were not publicly disclosed. item.title: Susan Collins Faces a Difficult Maine Senate Race Amid Voter Frustration With Trump
item.description: Senator Susan Collins, a Republican from Maine, is facing one of the most difficult political tests of her three-decade career as she seeks to retain her Senate seat. Collins has long built her electoral success on a reputation for moderation, independence, and attention to Maine’s specific interests, allowing her to win repeatedly in a state that usually supports Democratic presidential candidates. This election cycle, however, she is confronting a more challenging political environment shaped by voter anger over rising living costs, concerns about generational change in leadership, and opposition to President Trump’s second term. The article portrays Collins as a centrist figure whose conventional approach to politics may be under strain in a highly polarized era. At a fair in Fryeburg, Maine, she encountered both loyal supporters and voters who questioned whether she still represented the change they wanted. item.title: Diesel Futures Rise as Market Doubts Trump's Russia Deal Impact
item.description: Diesel futures prices have surged significantly, indicating potential further increases in diesel costs despite recent efforts by the Trump administration to lower prices. U.S. diesel futures rose 5% by midday on Tuesday, reaching their highest level in weeks, while European diesel futures climbed 3.8%. The average nationwide diesel price has increased by 70% since February 28, following U.S. and Israeli military actions against Iran. Gas prices have also risen over 45% during the same period. Analysts, including Gulf Oil adviser Tom Kloza and GasBuddy's Patrick De Haan, have noted 'stunning price spikes' in wholesale diesel, with retail prices potentially exceeding $6.53 per gallon. The Trump administration's recent deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to increase diesel supplies by purchasing previously sanctioned Russian reserves has been met with skepticism. item.title: Justice Department demands California verify voter citizenship within 48 hours ahead of midterms
item.description: The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) has issued a 48-hour demand to California Secretary of State Shirley Weber, requiring the state to verify the citizenship status of individuals identified as potential noncitizens before the midterm elections. The DOJ sent a letter and a password-protected thumb drive containing a list of names to California officials, instructing them to segregate ballots for these individuals and withhold counting until citizenship is confirmed. The letter, confirmed authentic by DOJ spokesperson Kiersten Pels, represents a significant escalation in the Trump administration's efforts to control state voting processes. The administration claims this is necessary to ensure election integrity, though experts and data from the Heritage Foundation indicate noncitizen voting is exceedingly rare. item.title: Astronomical Image Captures Milky Way Over Chilean Desert Sculpture
item.description: The Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) for October 13, 2026, features a stunning image titled 'Desert Stairway to Heaven' captured in the Atacama Desert of Chile. The photograph showcases a unique sculpture known as the Desert Staircase, positioned in the foreground with the Milky Way galaxy rising dramatically behind it. The image was taken in July 2025 and reveals several astronomical phenomena visible in the night sky. The Milky Way band appears near-vertical in the photograph, with the band of zodiacal light visible on the upper left. The green and red airglow can be seen just above the horizon, and the star Spica is visible within the zodiacal light stripe. At the top right of the image, the Small Magellanic Cloud galaxy is visible. The background includes the Andes Mountains, the Licancabur volcano, and the town lights of San Pedro de Atacama. item.title: Richarlison's Struggles Continue as Tottenham Keeps Him Out of Premier League Squad
item.description: Richarlison, Tottenham Hotspur's £60 million striker, has been left out of the Premier League squad for the 2026 season, making only his second appearance of the season in the EFL Trophy with the under-21s. The Brazilian forward, who was the team's leading scorer last season with 11 goals, has been unable to secure a transfer out of Tottenham despite expressing his desire to leave. His failed move to Everton and subsequent talks with Vasco da Gama fell through, leaving him without a clear path forward. Manager Roberto de Zerbi stated that the decision to omit Richarlison from the squad was not his, emphasizing that the player's own desire to depart was clear from the start of pre-season. Tottenham's attacking struggles have intensified, with the team scoring only three goals in the Premier League this season, placing them second bottom in the table. item.title: Kamala Harris' Advisor Defends Her Policy Proposals Amid 2028 Presidential Run Doubts
item.description: Kamala Harris, the former Vice President and Democratic presidential candidate, is facing growing skepticism within her party about her potential 2028 presidential bid. A longtime Democratic strategist and advisor, Maria Cardona, has pushed back against critics who argue that Harris has squandered her opportunity to reinvent herself following her 2024 election defeat. Cardona, a veteran of the Bill Clinton administration and current Democratic National Committee member, called the criticism 'infuriating in its silliness,' emphasizing Harris' policy proposals such as expanding the Supreme Court, lowering the voting age to 16, and making Washington D.C. and Puerto Rico states. These proposals, Cardona argued, represent groundbreaking initiatives that distinguish Harris from her 2024 campaign. item.title: Trump's Russia-Ukraine Policy Sparks GOP Concerns Amid Midterm Elections
item.description: President Donald Trump has engaged in a series of actions over the past five days that have drawn criticism from within his own party, particularly regarding his approach to Russia and Ukraine. The 80-year-old president announced a deal to lift sanctions on Russian diesel, allowing millions of tons of Russian fuel to enter global markets, which contradicts previous U.S. policy aimed at cutting off Moscow's war funding. This move followed a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, during which Trump also criticized Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky for strikes on Russian refineries and called for Ukraine to replace its leader. On Sunday, Trump declared an immediate 'energy ceasefire' without prior consultation, leaving Ukraine vulnerable to continued Russian attacks on its power grid. item.title: Trump Supporter Describes Trump Ally as 'Wicked, Evil Person' Yet Remains Loyal
item.description: The article discusses a revealing contradiction within the MAGA movement, centered around Eric Deters, a Kentucky attorney and longtime Trump donor. Deters claims that Kimberly Guilfoyle, Trump's ambassador to Greece and former fiancée of Donald Trump Jr., attempted to extort $100,000 from him through a direct wire transfer to her American Express account before her 2025 confirmation hearing. According to Deters, Guilfoyle suggested the payment would not appear on any records if sent directly to Amex, urging him to avoid creating a paper trail. Her attorney disputes the authenticity of these messages, but Deters insists the arrangement was a clear quid pro quo. Deters had previously paid Guilfoyle hundreds of thousands of dollars over the years, expecting her to leverage her connections within Trump's circle to assist him with various matters. item.title: Elissa Landi: A Regal Presence in 1930s Hollywood
item.description: Elissa Landi (1904–1948), born Elisabeth Marie Christine von Kühnelt in Venice, was an Austrian-Italian actress celebrated for her refined beauty and aristocratic demeanor in Hollywood films during the 1930s. Raised in Austria and educated in England, she began her career on the London stage before transitioning to American cinema. Landi gained recognition for her roles in notable films such as Cecil B. DeMille’s The Sign of the Cross (1932) and The Count of Monte Cristo (1934), where she starred alongside Robert Donat. Her elegant bearing and intelligent screen presence distinguished her as one of the most regal figures of the era. After retiring from acting in the early 1940s, Landi turned to writing novels and poetry, continuing to express her creative talents until her untimely death at age 43. item.title: Naomi Klein Warns of 'End Times Fascism' as Billionaires Prepare for Catastrophe
item.description: Naomi Klein, in a recent conversation with Doomscroll host Joshua Citarella, discusses what she and co-author Astra Taylor term 'end times fascism'—an emerging political alliance between religious fundamentalists anticipating Armageddon, tech oligarchs seeking to transcend humanity through technology, and nationalist movements constructing fortresses against displaced populations. Klein argues that decades of privatization, austerity policies, and corporate dominance have created the conditions for this political shift. She critiques the narrative promoted by tech billionaires who promise artificial intelligence will liberate humanity while simultaneously concentrating wealth and power, allowing them to decide whose lives are expendable. The article highlights how these elites are building private bunkers as a response to the very crises their policies have exacerbated, revealing a stark contrast between their public promises and private preparations. item.title: Banks and Financial Institutions Integrate AI Travel Assistants to Enhance Customer Experience
item.description:
Banks and financial institutions are increasingly leveraging artificial intelligence to integrate travel planning and payment services, aiming to capture a larger share of the travel spending market. Emirates NBD, in partnership with Visa and Tripadvisor, has launched a free AI travel assistant that anyone can use without a bank account. The tool utilizes Tripadvisor's extensive database of over 1 billion reviews and 8 million listings to create personalized itineraries based on user preferences, budget, and travel style. It also highlights Visa cardholder benefits such as hotel discounts and car rental perks, which could influence spending decisions. According to PYMNTS Intelligence, 70% of consumers change their purchasing decisions after seeing offers or rewards, and 43% switch payment methods to earn them.

item.title: Moss & Fog Introduces Color-Based Home Decor and Gift Collection
item.description: Moss & Fog, a visual culture destination that has been publishing since 2009, has launched a new feature on its website where home decor and gift items are organized by color. The platform has curated a collection of products that are sorted into eleven color categories: red, orange, gold, green, teal, blue, violet, pink, brown, night, and fog. Each color category features a selection of items that the Moss & Fog team has personally chosen for their aesthetic appeal and design quality. The collection includes items such as dinnerware, mugs, trays, soaps, and other home goods that are designed to be both functional and visually appealing. The website explains that the team selects each item one at a time, just as they select stories for their site, because it made them 'look twice.' The collection is part of Moss & Fog's broader mission to showcase beautiful, surprising, and thought-provoking work in art, architecture, design, and nature. item.title: Democrats Link Corruption to Rising Costs in 2026 Campaign Messaging
item.description: Democrats are increasingly framing government corruption as a direct cause of Americans’ economic difficulties, including high housing, health care, and living costs. According to a national survey conducted by Blue Rose Research and Democratic-aligned Winning Jobs Narrative Action, messaging that connected corruption to affordability increased support for Democratic congressional candidates by roughly three percentage points. The strategy represents a shift from treating corruption mainly as a threat to democratic norms or a criticism of President Donald Trump, toward presenting it as an explanation for voters’ everyday financial strain. Democratic candidates and strategists argue that a political system influenced by wealthy donors and corporate interests raises costs for ordinary households. Figures such as Sen. item.title: Cyberattack Forces French Supermarkets to Discard Food After Refrigeration Systems Overheat
item.description: Hackers remotely manipulated refrigeration-control systems at hundreds of supermarkets across France, forcing refrigerators and freezers into prolonged defrost cycles and raising temperatures to as high as 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit). The attack affected major retailers including Intermarché, Netto, Coopérative U, Carrefour, E.Leclerc and Monoprix, according to statements from the companies and French authorities. Les Mousquetaires, the owner of Intermarché, said about 150 of its stores were affected, with cooling units heated for roughly six hours overnight. Carrefour reported 80 affected supermarkets, while Coopérative U and Monoprix also confirmed disruption at portions of their store networks. Because the food could no longer be guaranteed safe, retailers discarded large quantities of fresh and frozen products, with early estimates suggesting losses could reach millions of euros. item.description: An 18-year-old woman has died following a crash involving an e-scooter in Caboolture, Queensland. The incident occurred on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, according to reports from The West Australian. The details surrounding the accident remain unclear, with no immediate information provided about the circumstances leading to the collision. Authorities are investigating the matter, and the community is mourning the loss of the young woman. The West Australian, a prominent newspaper in Western Australia, reported the incident as part of their ongoing coverage of local news. The article appears in the Queensland News section of the publication, highlighting the tragic event that has shaken the local community. item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that three strikes on Russian tech company Yandex's data centers had significantly reduced bot activity on social media platforms, making it 'a little easier to breathe' online. The strikes, which targeted data centers hosting Russian bot networks, coincided with a noticeable drop in engagement on Elon Musk's Twitter (now X) platform. Musk's posts, which previously averaged between 17,000 and 81,000 likes per day in October, saw a sharp decline to 11,000 and 8,000 likes over the past two days. While Cloudflare analysis showed a 99% drop in traffic from Yandex following the strikes, the company clarified that not all traffic was bot-related, including legitimate automated requests like search engine crawlers. Zelensky's office later walked back his initial claim, stating he was referring to the 'atmosphere' on social media rather than concrete evidence of reduced bot activity. item.title: Character.ai's Financial Struggles Highlight Unsustainable AI Business Models
item.description: Character.ai's bankruptcy filings reveal the financial challenges facing AI companies that rely on high operational costs without sustainable revenue models. The company spent $13.8 million monthly on AI compute in 2024, dropping to $10 million in 2025, while subscription revenue peaked at $2.8 million per month. Total revenue from all sources, including ads, reached $5.3 million monthly at its highest. Despite efforts to cut costs by simplifying AI models, laying off staff, and adding in-app advertising, the company reported losing $8-9 million monthly as of August 2026. Legal issues, including lawsuits over user harm and copyright infringement from Disney, contributed significantly to financial strain. CEO Colin Adams acknowledged the company's operational expenses were 'expensive to operate' and that profitability had been a long-standing challenge. item.title: Digger: A Climate Film That Challenges Audiences to Confront Power Dynamics
item.description: The article discusses the film 'Digger,' directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu and starring Tom Cruise, which has been critically panned and is considered a box-office failure. Despite its poor reception, the film is described as a profound exploration of climate change narratives and power structures. The movie presents a satirical play within a play, where Tom Cruise portrays an actor playing Digger Rockwell, a caricatured oil billionaire. The film's narrative reveals that the play 'Fossil Fools' depicts real historical events, creating a layered commentary on climate misinformation and corporate accountability. Unlike Adam McKay's 'Don't Look Up,' which posits that better communication of climate truths would lead to action, 'Digger' adopts a more nihilistic stance, suggesting that truth has little value in the face of entrenched capitalist interests. The film critiques the tendency to vilify specific figures like oil magnates while ignoring broader systemic issues. It also highli

item.title: Fifty Years After Ebola’s Discovery, Peter Piot Warns That Global Health Systems Remain Unprepared
item.description: Fifty years after helping identify the Ebola virus, Belgian scientist Dr. Peter Piot remains deeply concerned about the world’s ability to prevent and contain infectious-disease outbreaks. In 1976, Piot was a 27-year-old researcher at the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp when he examined blood samples sent from Yambuku, in what was then Zaire and is now the Democratic Republic of Congo. The samples came from a Flemish nun who had died of a mysterious illness. Under the microscope, Piot and colleagues saw an unusual, threadlike virus unlike typical spherical viruses. The pathogen was later named Ebola, after a nearby river, and the discovery involved Congolese doctors, local investigators, and researchers in Antwerp and Atlanta. The article also traces Piot’s later role in the HIV response. In the early 1980s, his work in Africa helped show that HIV was not confined to gay men, challenging a widespread misconception. He later became the first executive director of UNAIDS in 199

item.title: Childhood Struggles and Early Artistic Passion of Sir Roger Moore Revealed in Rare Photos
item.description: Sir Roger Moore's childhood, marked by health challenges, World War II hardships, and a deep love for the arts, is now being revealed through rare photographs from the 1920s and 1930s. Born on October 14, 1927, in Stockwell, London, Moore was the only child of George Alfred Moore, a London Metropolitan Police officer, and Lillian 'Lily' Pope, a homemaker. Despite the economic hardships of the Great Depression, his family enjoyed modest financial security due to his father's steady job. Moore's early years were characterized by frequent hospital visits due to severe illnesses, including double pneumonia, jaundice, and mumps. His parents' protective nature led him to develop a witty personality to handle bullying, a trait that later defined his acting style. During World War II, Moore and his family endured the Blitz, taking shelter in an Anderson shelter and evacuating to Devon. item.title: OpenAI Employee Allegedly Used AI Tools to Plan Covert Surveillance at Company Office
item.description: An OpenAI engineer, Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi Arabian national and U.S. permanent resident, is accused of using internal AI chatbots to plan and execute the covert placement of a recording device in an executive conference room at OpenAI's San Francisco office. According to a criminal complaint unsealed on October 13, 2026, Alfozan allegedly spent weeks querying an internal 'productivity agent' and an 'AI chatbot' to strategize the surveillance operation. He reportedly used an internal OpenAI tool to check meeting schedules in the targeted room and also utilized a chatbot account linked to his spouse to seek technical advice on setting up the device. The device, described as a Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense development board with a microphone and microSD storage, was concealed in toilet paper and placed behind a monitor in the conference room. item.title: Jon Ossoff rules out a 2028 presidential run and pledges to serve a full Senate term
item.description: Georgia Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff publicly ruled out a presidential campaign in 2028, saying during a Senate debate that he has “zero interest” in running for president and will instead seek reelection to the Senate. His comments came in response to a question from The Atlanta Journal-Constitution’s Greg Bluestein during a debate with Republican Representative Mike Collins. Ossoff also committed to serving a complete six-year Senate term if voters reelect him in November. The statement is his strongest public rejection so far of persistent speculation about a possible White House bid. Although his name has frequently appeared in discussions among national Democrats about potential contenders for the party’s 2028 presidential nomination, Ossoff has repeatedly sought to discourage that speculation. By explicitly pledging to remain in the Senate for the full term, he aimed to shift attention back to his reelection campaign in Georgia and reassure voters that he would not use the seat

item.title: FBI Arrests OpenAI Engineer After Hidden Recording Device Found in San Francisco Office
item.description: OpenAI said that the FBI arrested one of its employees after the company discovered a concealed recording device in one of its San Francisco offices. A security team conducting a sweep for surveillance equipment found the device on September 30 in a conference room. According to OpenAI, the device was designed to avoid detection, used advanced encryption, could capture audio, and had a method for transferring data without drawing attention. The Justice Department identified the employee as Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi Arabian national who joined OpenAI’s product team as an engineer in July 2025. Authorities said the device had been inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in one of OpenAI’s buildings. OpenAI said Alfozan allegedly intended to install additional recording devices in sensitive areas to secretly record meetings. The company said it used advanced AI models to help investigators examine copies of the data stored on the device and track changes to it.

item.title: Defender for Endpoint Day 3: Device Timeline, Inventory, and Vulnerability Management Explained
item.description: The article provides a detailed guide on using Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, focusing on Day 3 of the learning process. It covers device inventory, timeline analysis, and vulnerability management features. The author explains how to locate devices in the inventory, read device pages, investigate with the timeline, and understand vulnerability management capabilities. The article clarifies that Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 includes core vulnerability management, while additional features require an add-on.
